column8: Wed 18 Nov: store and Q&A only: Thorp's 3/4 growth for half the spread is right (checked at source), but the card itself shows IPS l.15's half is not a bet size (row 26), so never as the reason for the half; the spread halves, the variance quarters.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Thorp's 8 in 9 and 1 in 8 checked at source; the kept half is held, not rebalanced, and the plan sets no falls-to-half test, so it serves no part.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the bettor's twin of the case's over-promising warning (H5-011, H1-005 hold the decision rule); the lopsided cost comes from compounding, Laura's from trust, so a clause at most in Q&A.
Wed 18 Nov: Q&A for 3c if a judge raises Kelly: Kelly's own words tie the log rule to repeated bets, the source H5-011's single-shot point lacked; 3c's slot is Neyman, so not in the paragraph.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 4 (Kelly's own conditions for the log rule); the expectation rule it names is no guide for Laura either, as its own critique says.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Samuelson 1979 against log as a universal goal; its second quote restates the fallacy-of-large-numbers point already in H3-031 and Q39-016; 1971 read as an abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: store or a 3e clause: Thorp's 80 years for 98% at full Kelly and 6.7 and 26.7 years at half checked at source (r = 0, 10% growth, rebalanced); VT is bought and held three to five years, so never as a VT forecast.
Wed 18 Nov: store; a finite-run warning on a favourable coin bet; the plan states no share figure because IPS l.15 says whatever figure she chooses is money she already owns, not because of this.
Wed 18 Nov: store; quantile Kelly lands where IPS l.11 does (promised money takes no share risk); niche and verified, but a bettor's quantile of wealth after many bets, so a parallel for Q&A only.
Wed 18 Nov: store; kills claim B (half is common practice, not a standard); the Keynes and Buffett fractions are Ziemba's estimates as cited, never read at source.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Baker and McHale's shrink factor shows half answers one ratio of error to edge; a formula, hard to say plainly, and Laura is not betting repeatedly.
Wed 18 Nov: true simulation figures, but the use is wrong: 3c states owned figures because IPS l.15 says so, not because of a mean-median gap; store only, with that reason struck.
Wed 18 Nov: the frame behind row 14 for 3b and 3e: a fractional bettor's half guards against too high an estimate of the edge (read at source with quotes); the plan's stated figures use no estimate.

Wed 18 Nov: figures match NUMBERS 4 exactly ($115,000 top in every column, half kept $17,949 to $23,759) but repeat Q37-018 and AHA row 7; the Kelly frame is new; fix the error lands only in money promised to no one: true for steady returns on the central path at forwards and any above about 3.4% a year (8p; 4% clears the step by $296; GMO and Ninety One give $110,000, 13 of 15); market luck before the move still moves the top ($95,000 to $140,000, house 1-in-20, section 4; TNA l.21).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e in words: errors in the mean cost most, and the stated figures use no mean (Chopra and Ziemba as cited); the 7.5% still sets Table 2's spread and her flexibility, so say the stated figures, never the plan, do not use it.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Thorp's g = -.75 when the true edge is half the estimate and 1.5 times the estimated Kelly is bet, checked at source; no promised dollar is sized on VT's estimate.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Benter's quote verified, but the 0.72 and 0.37 for Laura are Keel arithmetic on J.P. Morgan's figures, S 3 at most, never plan figures.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; Benter's record shows fractional Kelly pays over hundreds of bets a year; the press account is secondary; serves no part.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b or 2.0 erudition: Benter's effective wealth is less than their actual current wealth is IPS l.11 (quoted exactly: only money you haven't promised yet goes into shares) in a bettor's words; the plan goes further, taking promised money out of shares entirely.

Wed 18 Nov: Q&A only: inputs match NUMBERS (J.P. Morgan 7.50 / 8.94 / 17.88, CANON B15; 1-year 4.33%; IBTM 4.86%) and 1.44, 1.28, about 1.5 and 0.69 recompute; Keel arithmetic on a 10-15 year forecast J.P. Morgan says is not for short-term decisions; margin is banned.

Wed 18 Nov: Q&A for 3b: plan figures match NUMBERS ($81,244, $29,594, $21,179, $143,682) and 26.7%, 14.7%, 6.6%, 0.19, 0.10 recompute (Keel arithmetic, never plan figures); fix the cause: VT's 26.7% of the 2028 money is set by IPS l.15's Most and the rest (Keel's 73.3% reading), what is left after the payments by l.11 and l.13; it hands critics too timid, so never lead with it.
Wed 18 Nov: store; 2.1 times the edge, about 3.5 and 15 years and 0.87 recompute (Keel arithmetic on Rising and Wyner); a simple-average error model, so Q&A only.

Wed 18 Nov: store; 4.4% compound and 0.23 at the panel median recompute (Keel arithmetic, one period, J.P. Morgan's spread applied to every house); the median is said as about 6.5%, J.P. Morgan's 7.5% above it, correctly.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Thorp's Berkshire inputs and f* = 6.22 checked at source (0.16 is its reciprocal); answers a fifth of Kelly is fear in Q&A only.

Wed 18 Nov: Q&A only: half Kelly as risk aversion 2 makes half a stated taste; 3b's defence stays NUMBERS 8o's trade (each $5,000 more of top costs about $5,300 of what she keeps), Caplet's choice, never optimal.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b: the half is money promised to no one for IPS l.15's three uses, split on a known value before the meetings (CANON A30-A32 checked; contribution equals the stated top in every path, NUMBERS 4); mostly restates SKELETON 3b, the new part is not a bet size.

Wed 18 Nov: $365 to $1,087 match NUMBERS 8o; replace about two years on about $18,000 (not a NUMBERS figure, and the split shifts only part of the moved half) with 8o's own reason: the total is linear in the share moved, so the split decides what is promised, not how much there is.
Wed 18 Nov: store housekeeping: H3-118 is already merged into H1-005, whose note voids the old 3-in-4; this row adds the reason (the stated top is owned, NUMBERS 4 and 8o).
Wed 18 Nov: store; biology's verified twin of H5-002 and the Cohen rows (a floor makes the long-run rule the wrong guide); the plan's floor answer is structural, as IPS l.11 says.
Wed 18 Nov: store; abstract only; the 13 of 15 houses giving $115,000 matches NUMBERS 8p as re-sized; the mapping of the market's belief to the houses' panel is loose.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c contrast: Granger's mean plus a bias, a quantile under straight-line costs (through Christoffersen and Diebold, read at source), the econometric twin of the store's newsvendor rows; Laura states owned figures, not a quantile.
Wed 18 Nov: store; under LINEX the lean grows with uncertainty (NBER paper read at source); the plan avoids choosing a lean by stating only owned figures.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c: the Fed's 4-to-1 lean is a stated choice; Laura's lean is the rule's own (zero interest, the 0.5% cut, rounding down: $115,000 stated against $122,503 the funds pay centrally, NUMBERS 4), named as a choice, never prudent.

Wed 18 Nov: the forecaster facts hold, but the use is wrong: the bottom is owned from January 2028, not a lean, and 3d leads with the top co-sponsors count (funder test, 16 Nov); use only as row 39's contrast or beside row 33.

Wed 18 Nov: Rockefeller read at source; keep the most accurate estimate is not always the best estimate as row 36's first clause, and drop as a range told by its bottom does: 3d leads with the top and says the bottom once.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c contrast and a reserve aha candidate: states that usually under-forecast still over-forecast in the downturn (more than 70% in fiscal 2009), the years co-sponsors' budgets can fall; the review says the errors may not be deliberate, so never shading caused it.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 35 (public budgets lean low), on secondary citations except Krol's abstract.
Wed 18 Nov: store; the pull to the middle persists with known odds and training (replication confirms); a rule fixed on owned money takes judgment out of the meeting room, a 3c Q&A line.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c's frame: shade a forecast, shrink a bet, or state only what is owned (IPS l.15, checked), and only the last holds in a downturn; say it of what Laura states after the move, since the report's about $95,000 to $115,000 on today's figures is the rule's value today, not a promise (NUMBERS 4).
Wed 18 Nov: a written reason (Book 17): fractional Kelly stays out of 3f; Kelly is not in the team's record and its numbers side with the too-timid critics.
